chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.
chapter_note: The opening third is dominated by hagiographic Q&A frame and explicit Gospel/NT proof-texting (overlay). The oldest layer emerges from ¶11 onward as systematic five-fold mappings (intellectual faculties ↔ cosmic beings/ships ↔ ascent process) and dualist mechanics, with two clear institutional/editorial grafts (¶13, ¶16) flagged by seam-like register shift to holy church/catechumens/alms. The ending returns to a compact dualist creedal-logic in core voice (¶24–26), with a final beatitude fragment (¶27) likely continuing the same core cadence.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief heading-like lead-in with 'they asked/besought him' narrative setup; pure frame voice.
Contains disciples' request + explicit Gospel citation formula 'As it is written in the Gospel' and the Lukan parable text; enters via NT proof-texting even though embedded in frame.
Continues entreaty + 'it is written ... scriptures' citation register; functions as scriptural proof-text request rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Sets up controversy 'some among the sects explain' in a reporting voice; not yet the systematic cosmological teaching proper.

Explicit hagiographic speaker-intro 'Then speaks our master Manichaios, the apostle of greatness' plus polemical narrative about sectarian explanation; the didactic core is not presented in systematic mapping yet.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.18⟩ [ ... ] their child, as it strikes [ ... ] while first one [ ... ] in them [ ... ] at the end there is one [ ... ] it occurs in its fibres and its branches [ ... ] There is a bad dust in them [ ... ] date palm [ ... ] before the tree that [ ... ] bad; because they give the decision [ ... ] the one that they name [ ... ] the type [ ... ] name it: tree [ ... ] is sweet [ ... ] writing [ ... ] they shall establish [ ... ] man [ ... ] it is sweet [ ... ] seed of the [ ... ] and it is used for their nourishment [ ... ] will explain [ ... ] may not join to the [ ... ] mankind, as they are named [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite lacunae, the paragraph reads as impersonal explanatory mechanics about mixture/composite nature using a concrete analogy (date palm) rather than citation; no institutional markers.
NT narrative exemplum: Judas among the twelve, 'Satan entered him', handing saviour to Jews, crucifixion; enters via Gospel/NT tradition.
Continues Judas Iscariot exemplum; purely NT narrative overlay.
Paul persecuting the church then revelation—specific NT/Acts-derived biographical exemplum even if used to argue mixture; overlay by entry vector.
Uses 'the saviour preached in the parable' as authority cue; continues NT-anchored parable framing rather than direct cosmological mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] how I will reveal to you [ ... ] the expound[er ... ] the trees [ ... ] the Father [ ... ] all of them, as he [ ... ] in the [ ... ] world [ ... ] this good tree, the [ ... ] the light of this good tree [ ... ] the Pillar [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Transition into direct revelatory exposition with cosmic referents (Father, light, Pillar) and no citation formula; beginning of the systematic teaching layer though fragmentary.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.20⟩ ... the intellectuals that are cloaked upon its body [ ... ] this good tree. They are the light elements that are mingled, being compounded in the totality.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Characteristic core diction: 'intellectuals', body-cloaking, light elements mingled/compounded—process/mechanics voice.
Seam-like institutional extension (holy church, teachers, catechumens) appended to the tree scheme; even with 'Jesus the Splendour' the paragraph’s function is ecclesial identification of 'taste'.

paragraphs.core_text: Behold, this is the good tree [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Deictic closure marking the defined referent; fits as a core hinge into the five-limb definition.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] I reveal to you [ ... ] it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.] [Its counsel] is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. [Its insight is the Fir]st Man who dwells in the ship of living waters. Its thought is the Third Ambassador [who dwells in] the ship of living fire, that shines in [ ... ] Also, the mind is the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the clause 'Its consideration is the holy church.' as an institutional identification (ecclesial graft) inside an otherwise systematic five-fold cosmological mapping.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is the numbered five-limb map correlating intellectual faculties to named cosmic beings/ships. One embedded ecclesial identification ('holy church') disrupts the cosmological sequence, indicating later insertion inside a core paragraph.
Institutional/cultic practice (alms, catechumens, holy church, purification) with seam-flagged register shift; editorial pastoral extension.

paragraphs.core_text: It is consideration that shall [ ... ] they shall be raised up [ ... ] is counsel; they shall be raised up to insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night; from insight they shall rise up to thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day. And he too, great glorious thought, shall bring them in to mind; which is the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process-oriented ascent mechanics (faculty-to-faculty ladder) mapped onto cosmic beings/ships; impersonal systematic core voice.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the good tree that shall give good fruit, [ ... ] is the entire life and light for ever [ ... ] occurs [ ... ] ever, it is blessed [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the definitional scheme in impersonal doxological-cosmological register ('life and light for ever') without ecclesial or NT citation apparatus.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.21⟩ [ ... ] bad [ ... ] happen in [ ... ] from [ ... ] also [ ... ] the way that it is [ ... ] the good tree [ ... ] of the fire [ ... ] they are the ruling-power [ ... ] heaven and the wheel [ ... ] they are the five fleshes that walk [ ... ] fruit [ ... te]aching as of error, the mystery that [ ... wh]ich Satan appointed in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Moves into the negative counterpart with cosmic/astral terms (heaven, wheel, ruling-power) and Satan as cosmological agent; still expository rather than institutional.

paragraphs.core_text: However, the taste of these bad fruits is these evil people, the sects [ ... wh]ich are bound in law after law, they and their teachers [ ... ] the law of death; they taking taste for it, they being thirsty for it [ ... ] the souls of death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Anti-sect polemic is integrated as the negative 'taste' within the tree-correspondence system ('law of death'); not church-rule material, so best read as part of the older explanatory schema (with some uncertainty).
Returns to 'our master called' + 'in the scriptures' appeal; reattaches the scheme to scriptural authority, suggesting later proof-texting overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.22⟩ [ ... I will] reveal to you and you [ ... ] The bad tree has five limbs. They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind. Its consideration is the law of death from which the sects take instruction. Its counsel is transmigration [ ... ] in type after type. Also, its insight is the furnaces of fire [ ... ge]henna; which is full of smoke. Thought [ ... ] vessel. Its mind is the [ ... ] the lump, the last bond, the [ ... ], they that Satan cast away [ ... ] the great [ ... ] and they fall [ ... ] the darkness [ ... ] all [ ... ] and they take away [ ... ] are swallowed in to the lump, and they are bound [ ... ] the fruit of darkness, the one that they [ ... ] for ever and ever [ ... ] his face [ ... ] will arrive at that place; and they have no repentance therein.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Full systematic five-fold negative mapping (faculties ↔ eschatological/cosmic stations: transmigration, furnaces/gehenna, vessel, lump/last bond) in impersonal explanatory voice; no NT citation formula despite 'gehenna' term.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] this is the explanation of the bad tree, as I have explained to you, which you [ ... ] to it [ ... ] good fruit [ ... ] its fruit bad [ ... ] in it, in its existent days [ ... ] in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Internal closure of the exposition ('this is the explanation... as I have explained'); aligns with core teaching cadence.

paragraphs.core_text: Concerning this [ ... ] and my beloved ones [ ... ] them in truth, it being changed from [ ... ] which lies in its good earth [ ... life] and light; as death and darkness do not exist [ ... ] Also, the bad tree is Matter [ ... ] it, I understand it alone among the [ ... wh]ich occurs in its bad earth [ ... ] darkness and death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Semi-creedal dualist assertion in cosmological ontology terms (Matter; life/light vs death/darkness; two 'earths'); core doctrinal voice.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.23⟩ Blessed is every one [ ... ] these two trees, and separates them one from another. He understands that they did not arise out of one another, nor did they come from one another. They did not come from one! The person who can separate them out may go up to the aeon of light, [ ... as I have] revealed it to you.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding beatitude-like exhortation tightly tied to ontological dualism and ascent ('aeon of light'); not institutional regulation.

paragraphs.core_text: And he sees [ ... ] bad fruit did not arise from it [ ... ]; but whoever will not separate out [ ... ] from one another, he falls to the land of darkness [ ... ] until he arrives at the [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct consequence logic (separate → ascent / fail → land of darkness) consistent with core dualist mechanics.

paragraphs.core_text: Blessed is whoever can believe! He [ ... ] darkness; which grows out of the [ ... ] for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary final beatitude continuing the core dualist cadence; no frame closure or church-institution markers preserved.
